title: Median of [10, 9, 2] is 2
explanation: Default sort() compares values as strings, so [10, 9, 2] becomes [10, 2, 9]. It also sorts the caller's array in place.
hint: What does sort() compare by when you pass no function?

title: Cart total is "[object Object]25"
prompt: With two items in stock, the total comes back as a string.
explanation: With no initial value, the first sum is the first cart object, and object + number concatenates as strings. An empty array would throw a TypeError instead.
hint: What is sum on the very first call?

title: Every node is connected to everything
explanation: fill([]) creates one array and puts that same array in every slot, so every push goes to the shared list. Array.from with a factory makes a new array per slot.

title: Visited set never matches
prompt: Grid DFS never stops: visit(0, 0) returns true every time.
explanation: Sets compare objects by reference. Every [r, c] literal is a brand-new array, so has never finds a match. Use a string key like '0,0', or r * cols + c.
hint: Are two arrays with the same contents equal to each other?

title: Two sum misses index 0
explanation: The stored index can be 0, which is falsy, so the check fails exactly when the match is the first element. Check for undefined, or use a Map with has().
hint: Which stored value would make that if fail even though it exists?

title: getName(null) throws
prompt: getName(null) throws a TypeError instead of returning 'unknown'.
explanation: typeof null is 'object', a bug kept for backwards compatibility. Any "is object" check needs an explicit !== null.

title: Highest score is 9, not 10
explanation: split returns strings, and strings compare character by character, so '9' > '10'. Convert to numbers first.
hint: What type are the items split returns?
